Fabianhaza Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Micsurin utca 1, Hungary

Demolished. Fábiánháza's Jewish community, settled around 1800 with permission from the landowning Count Károlyi family, was Orthodox and fell under the jurisdiction of the Mátészalka Jewish community for most of its existence, maintaining a synagogue, burial society, yeshiva, and Talmud Torah. At midnight on April 12, 1944, the village's Jews were rounded up on accusations of hiding a secret radio transmitter in the synagogue, then transferred to the Mátészalka Ghetto, which held about 18,000 Jews from the surrounding area before deportation to Auschwitz weeks later. This cemetery existed by 1892, per that year's cadastral map.
